title: "Sankey / alluvial diagrams in JavaScript with CanvasXpress"
description: "Show how quantities flow through a sequence of stages — cohort to treatment to outcome — as an interactive Sankey diagram in the browser, from one portable spec."
author: "Isaac Neuhaus"

---

A Sankey (or alluvial) diagram shows how a quantity **flows through a sequence of categorical
stages** — patients moving from a cohort, to a treatment, to an outcome. The width of each stream is
the magnitude. CanvasXpress is a JavaScript library at heart, so in the browser it's just a `data`
object and a `config`.

## Load the library

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
```

## The markup and the spec

Each row is one path through the stages; the value (`Freq`) is the single variable, and the stages
are sample annotations (`x`). `sankeyAxes` lists the stages in order.

```html
<canvas id="sankey" width="700" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
  var cohorts = ["Cohort A", "Cohort B"],
      treats  = ["Drug 1", "Drug 2", "Placebo"],
      outcomes = ["Response", "Stable", "Progression"];

  var Cohort = [], Treatment = [], Outcome = [], Freq = [];
  cohorts.forEach(function (co) {
    treats.forEach(function (tr) {
      outcomes.forEach(function (ou) {
        var base = ou === "Response" ? 40 : ou === "Stable" ? 25 : 15;
        if (tr === "Placebo" && ou === "Response") base = 12;   // placebo responds less
        Cohort.push(co); Treatment.push(tr); Outcome.push(ou);
        Freq.push(base + Math.floor(Math.random() * 16));
      });
    });
  });

  var ids = Freq.map(function (_, i) { return "r" + (i + 1); });

  var data = {
    y: { vars: ["Freq"], smps: ids, data: [Freq] },
    x: { Cohort: Cohort, Treatment: Treatment, Outcome: Outcome }
  };

  var config = {
    graphType: "Sankey",
    sankeyAxes: ["Cohort", "Treatment", "Outcome"],
    xAxis: ["Freq"],
    colorBy: "Outcome",
    sankeyType: "proportional",
    graphOrientation: "horizontal",
    title: "Patient flow: cohort to treatment to outcome"
  };

  new CanvasXpress("sankey", data, config);
</script>
```

## Live result

```{=html}
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@69.6.1/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<canvas id="sankeyLive" width="700" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
(function () {
  function draw() {
    if (typeof CanvasXpress === "undefined") { return setTimeout(draw, 60); }
    var cohorts = ["Cohort A", "Cohort B"], treats = ["Drug 1", "Drug 2", "Placebo"],
        outcomes = ["Response", "Stable", "Progression"];
    var Cohort = [], Treatment = [], Outcome = [], Freq = [];
    cohorts.forEach(function (co) {
      treats.forEach(function (tr) {
        outcomes.forEach(function (ou) {
          var base = ou === "Response" ? 40 : ou === "Stable" ? 25 : 15;
          if (tr === "Placebo" && ou === "Response") base = 12;
          Cohort.push(co); Treatment.push(tr); Outcome.push(ou);
          Freq.push(base + Math.floor(Math.random() * 16));
        });
      });
    });
    var ids = Freq.map(function (_, i) { return "r" + (i + 1); });
    new CanvasXpress("sankeyLive",
      { y: { vars: ["Freq"], smps: ids, data: [Freq] },
        x: { Cohort: Cohort, Treatment: Treatment, Outcome: Outcome } },
      { graphType: "Sankey", sankeyAxes: ["Cohort", "Treatment", "Outcome"], xAxis: ["Freq"],
        colorBy: "Outcome", sankeyType: "proportional", graphOrientation: "horizontal",
        title: "Patient flow: cohort to treatment to outcome" });
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

Hover any stream to see the count; the widths are proportional to the frequency. `sankeyType` can
also be `"aligned"` (classic alluvial) or `"equal"`.

## Why "reproducible"

The `data`+`config` **is** the figure — one portable JSON spec that renders the same from R, Python,
or a web page.
